numerical_failure.observed_behavior: In the float branch, `sequence_to_td64ns` converts `OutOfBoundsDatetime` to `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` unconditionally, never consulting `errors`, so `pd.to_timedelta(..., errors='coerce')` does not coerce to `NaT` for float-dtype ndarray/Series/masked-EA inputs the way the object path and sibling conversions do. Separately, in the `Timedelta` kwargs path, `int()` of a non-finite float raises a bare `OverflowError` instead of producing `OutOfBoundsTimedelta`.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Respect `errors`: under `errors='raise'` re-raise as `OutOfBoundsTimedelta`, and under `errors='coerce'` fall back to the element-wise path that honors `errors='coerce'` (yielding `NaT`/`NaT`-equivalent). For `Timedelta` kwargs with non-finite floats, produce `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` rather than a bare `OverflowError`.
trigger_conditions: `pd.to_timedelta` / `sequence_to_td64ns` float branch with float-dtype ndarray/Series/masked EA input containing out-of-bounds datetime magnitude (e.g. `[1.5, 1e30]` seconds) while `errors='coerce'`
`pd.Timedelta` kwargs path called with a non-finite float (e.g. `np.inf`), where the implementation previously used `int()` leading to a bare `OverflowError`

oracle_clues: Float-branch bug described as: it converts `OutOfBoundsDatetime` to `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` unconditionally, never consulting `errors`, so it diverges from object path and sibling paths when `errors='coerce'`.
Expected `errors='coerce'` behavior is shown by the object path example: `pd.to_timedelta([1.5, 1e30], unit="s", errors="coerce")  # [1.5s, NaT]`.
Fix description: only re-raise `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` when `errors == 'raise'`; otherwise fall back to element-wise path that honors `errors='coerce'`.

Separate kwargs-path failure oracle: `pd.Timedelta(days=np.inf)` previously raised a bare `OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer`; expected behavior is `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` (positional path already right for `pd.Timedelta(np.inf, unit="D")`).

category_specific_evidence: Special values involved (explicit): non-finite floats `np.inf` and `-np.inf`.

Where they enter: `pd.Timedelta(days=np.inf)` and `Timedelta(**{kwarg: val})` with `kwarg` in {`weeks`,`days`,`hours`,`minutes`,`seconds`,`milliseconds`,`microseconds`,`nanoseconds`} and `val` in {`np.inf`,`-np.inf`}.
Problem in kwargs path: `int()` of a non-finite float raised a bare `OverflowError` instead of raising/producing `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` (PR#66823 / test and code comments).
Correct handling for kwargs/non-finite floats: for `Timedelta(**{kwarg: val})`, tests expect `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` with message matching “Cannot construct Timedelta”.

Where “errors” handling enters: float-branch `sequence_to_td64ns` previously converted `OutOfBoundsDatetime` to `OutOfBoundsTimedelta` unconditionally, “never consulting errors”, so `pd.to_timedelta(..., errors="coerce")` diverged from object/list and sibling paths (object path shown as yielding `[1.5s, NaT]` while float-branch yielded `OutOfBoundsTimedelta`).
Correct handling for float-branch: “re-raise only under `errors=\"raise\"`, otherwise fall back to the element-wise path that honors `errors=\"coerce\"` (yielding `NaT`/`NaT`-equivalent)”.

Evidence of non-finite float `errors`-coercion expectation: `test_float_inf_raises` asserts that `errors="coerce"` results in `NaT` (and the test name indicates the non-finite inputs are `np.inf` and `-np.inf`).
reproduction_risks: `NaN`, signed zero, and subnormals are not mentioned in the provided passages; only `+inf` and `-inf` are evidenced as special values.
Dtype/precision/magnitude regime/tolerance are not stated anywhere in the supplied passages for this special-value behavior; using inferred tolerances or precision would be speculative (leave null).

The failure is explicitly tied to the `sequence_to_td64ns` float branch for `errors` handling and separately to the `Timedelta` kwargs `int()` path for non-finite floats; reproductions that only test one path may miss the other issue.
